flags.headline: Hormuz conflict escalates further — third consecutive night of US-Iran strikes, ceasefire fractured, Brent above $87 — now confirmed in the book's energy-sleeve price action
flags.detail: Escalation continues from yesterday's flag: U.S. forces carried out a third consecutive night of strikes against Iran; the ceasefire/ MoU reached last month has fractured; President Trump reinstated a blockade of Iranian shipping and proposed a 20% fee to guard the Strait of Hormuz. Ship-tracking data shows transits through the Strait at their lowest level in two months (57 transits Fri-Sun, >50% below the prior week's pace). Brent crude is above $87/bbl (+4.45% today on top of +9.6% Monday, now +19% versus its pre-conflict level); WTI is near $81 (+3.34%). Unlike yesterday's pre-market read (still pricing Friday's close), today's data drop reflects live pricing and confirms the energy sleeve responding: VLO +5.41%, DVN +3.52%, CVX +3.33%, OKE +2.57%, CNX +1.13% (natural-gas name, smaller Hormuz linkage, smaller move). The same energy shock is feeding into Fed policy expectations: June CPI prints at 8:30am ET today (consensus 3.8%, cooling), but odds of a Fed rate HIKE (not cut) at the July 28-29 meeting have risen to ~43%, and September hike odds on CME FedWatch have jumped to ~76% from 57% a week ago, as escalating energy costs keep inflation risk elevated even as headline CPI cools. Bank earnings season also opens today (JPM, GS, WFC, C) — a macro tone-setter with no direct held-name overlap. Direction for the energy sleeve remains genuinely two-sided long-term (upstream/refining benefit from higher prices; broader risk-off and rate-hike risk are negative for growth multiples), but the magnitude and stacking of catalysts (war escalation + CPI + bank earnings + Fed repricing) keeps this at RED for gap/event risk, not because any single held name's thesis has broken.

evidence.source: CNBC — U.S. crude jumps above $80 as Iran ceasefire fractures; Trump's Hormuz toll plans reignite supply fears
